summary: An inaugural point opens by setting what was against what is, or them against us, then ends on a belief or an image.
realLife: About one inaugural point in eight opens on a contrast: then and now, the crisis and the answer, or a faith kept despite the doubters. It usually ends on a belief or an image, not an ask.
sources: Franklin D. Roosevelt, first inaugural address, Mar 4, 1933: https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/inaugural-address-8
George W. Bush, first inaugural address, Jan 20, 2001: https://teachingamericanhistory.org/document/first-inaugural-address-gwbush/
Read in full and coded point by point in docs/story/research/address-moves.md (Elections lane, Nov 24, 2026); that note is an extra line, the speeches are the sources.
inGame: the stance engine gives the speaker's side and the other side's position on the question; the law in force and the term's records give the then and the now
